extracted.intended_audience: makers and 3D designers (OpenSCAD/Thingiverse) creating randomized fills for 3D-printable models
extracted.subtask_description: Create an OpenSCAD/STL design that fills a prismatic volume with randomly distributed and sized objects that remain inside the volume and are printable. The workflow covers position math, collision/overlap control, reproducible randomness, rotation for distribution, and postprocessing for printability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random distribution and sizing of objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Fill a prismatic volume with randomly distributed and sized objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use randomness to place and scale items so the volume appears filled; aim for visually even/random coverage. The author notes this as the primary design idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute positions so points lie within triangular cross-section
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive x and y positions from two lines dividing two corners so that the crossover point always lays within the triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform trigonometric calculations to map random samples into the triangular domain so placed objects are inside the triangle rather than outside or on edges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt placement region to object size
rubrics_metrics.description: Alter the triangle in size depending on the object's size so that the object always lays within the volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shrink/offset the allowable placement area by the object's bounds (half-extents/radius) to prevent geometry from crossing the prism boundary; this was implemented by the author ("done").

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent objects protruding out top and bottom
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix objects that pop out on top and bottom of the prism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure z-coordinate and object heights are constrained within the prism caps; author marked this as fixed in updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-calculation tuning for overlaps and connections (3D-printability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform postcalculation to tune overlaps and connections to make the assembly 3D printable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust tolerances, overlaps, and connection geometry after placement so parts are sufficiently connected or separated for printing and assembly; author notes this as partially complete ("halfway done").

rubrics_metrics.name: Collision detection / distance control
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects only placed within a certain distance (negative for allowed overlap).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement collision checks or minimum-distance constraints during placement to avoid unwanted intersections or to allow controlled overlap; introduced in Update V2 as 'collision detection!'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply rotation per iteration for better distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a vector rotation every iteration for better distribution of objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotate placement vectors or objects incrementally to avoid alignment artifacts and produce more even spatial spread; introduced in Update V3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use custom seeds for reproducible randomness
rubrics_metrics.description: Support custom seeds so randomness is reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow the user to set random seeds to recreate specific distributions; noted as added in Update V3 ('custom seeds (reproducible randomness, yeah)').

rubrics_metrics.name: Document progress, versions, and known issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide update notes listing implemented features and remaining work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log changes (e.g., V2 collision detection, V3 rotation and seeds), outstanding tasks (e.g., postcalculation tuning), and what is 'done' vs 'halfway done' so users know stability and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: License and metadata clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish usage/license and descriptive metadata with the design (Attribution 4.0 International, topics, file size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear licensing, tags (openscad, stl, thingiverse, random), file size and identifiers so downstream users know reuse rights and can find/assess the item.
